title: pvWarpByVector
body:
## pvWarpByVector

Displaces each point by ScaleFactor × a 3-component point vector (x' = x + ScaleFactor · v), e.g. structural displacements or mode shapes, to show the deformed shape. Polydata, structured and unstructured grids keep their type; image and rectilinear inputs become structured grids. Point and cell data pass through, but input normals are dropped because the geometry changed. The curated warpVector covers the common case.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Use a ScaleFactor of 1 for true displacements; larger factors exaggerate deformation, so state the factor in published images.
- Recompute normals after warping for correct shading.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `WarpByVector`. Identity: `filters/WarpVector`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the filter. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 3 components. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
